headline: Majors hold 200-day lines with all four momentum indicators flat, but whales are loading onto exchanges while retail greed sits at 69.
paragraphs: The regime is intact but not accelerating. All seven majors remain above their 200-day moving averages, and six of seven carry golden crosses (XRP and ADA are the exceptions, both marooned below the 200-line). But every single momentum indicator is in neutral: RSI-14 across the tape runs 48 to 58, the dead center of the board, and MACD is negative on every asset. This is a trend that is still alive but has stopped pushing. Bitcoin down 1.6% on the day but up 21.1% on the month. Ethereum down 1.5% on the day but up 33.3% on the month. The weekly and monthly windows tell different stories on every single name, which is the tell: the move has legs, but the tape is tired today.

Positioning reveals a market bracing for friction. Bitcoin funding stands at 8.9% annualized; Ethereum at 1.0%. Both are positive, meaning long holders are paying to hold, but Bitcoin's cost is four times higher, a sign that conviction on spot has thinned relative to the derivatives market. More telling: Bitcoin's open interest sits at 2.2 billion USD, but the long-short ratio is 1.73, meaning there is real dry powder on the short side. On altcoins the picture warps. Solana funding is negative 10.5% annualized while the long-short ratio hits 2.14, a rare state: shorts are being paid to hold because longs are so dominant that the market is hungry for supply. XRP shows 9.9% funding annualized with a 2.49 long-short ratio; Dogecoin's long-short ratio explodes to 4.68 on 4.7% funding. These are crowded bets on the alts. When positioning is this lopsided, liquidations matter. Over the last 5 to 17 hours, Bitcoin has seen 100 liquidations worth 1.1 million in long value versus 8.5 thousand in shorts. Ethereum: 140 thousand longs liquidated, 29 thousand shorts. Solana: 796 thousand longs, 6.4 thousand shorts. The asymmetry is loud.

Flows paint the real story. Over the last 24 hours, whales moved 238 million USD onto exchanges: 77 million Bitcoin to Binance, 74 million Ethereum to Coinbase Institutional, 64 million Ethereum to Coinbase. This is not panic selling off; this is accumulation into venues. The weekly trend confirms it: the week ending September 15 saw 890 million move onto exchanges, the largest single week since August 25 (1.04 billion). Four straight weeks of consistent inflow to venues. Meanwhile, stablecoins sit at 310 billion USD, up 1.36% on the month, dry powder that has actually grown. The contradiction is specific: spot ETF flows on Bitcoin show 159.9 million inflow on September 14, but the five-session net is negative 302.8 million, same direction days just one. ETF flows have reversed at the margin. On Ethereum, the reverse is true: 121.1 million on the 14th and 318 million inflow over five sessions, both pointing into the same door. Traditional finance is staying in Ethereum; it is stepping back on Bitcoin even as whales load spot onto exchanges.

Sentiment sits at 69, squarely in greed territory, but the tape does not match the crowd's calm. Fear and Greed has ranged 31 to 74 over thirty days, so 69 is well into the upper half; yet every momentum indicator is flat, and the market structure suggests distribution into the rally, not new buying power. The largest 24-hour drawdown since the move began was Bitcoin down 1.6%, Ethereum down 1.5%, broad and shallow. Total market cap is down 3.34% on the day to 2.65 trillion USD, a pullback, but Bitcoin dominance has actually ticked up to 58.3%, a sign that Bitcoin weakness is softer than the altseason narrative would suggest.

Watch three conditions. First, whether the long-short liquidation asymmetry persists: Bitcoin and Ethereum seeing ten-to-twenty times more long liquidations than shorts is structural stress on leverage; if that ratio normalizes, the crowding has begun to clear. Second, the 200-day hold on Dogecoin and Cardano: both are below the line, both are weak on the month despite the broader rally, and both carry extreme per-30-day volatility (78% and 83% respectively). If either reclaims the 200-line with real conviction, the entire alt structure has better footing. Third, the divergence in ETF flows: Bitcoin flows have turned outward on the five-day window even as whales load spot. If that reversal persists, it flags a potential fork in traditional-finance and whale capital direction.
